source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed advertised specifications in a consumer product performance report

1. Start with the test records.
2.
completion:
Review the test methods as published in ASTM.
3. Review the published performance criteria in ASTM.
4. Assess the reported test results in the form of numerical values or qualitative results.
5. Match the reported results against the published criteria.
6. Report whether the test passed or failed in the consumer product performance report.
If the method produced a numerical result and had published performance criteria, then use the word "met" to indicate whether the reported result was to the right of (>) the published performance criteria (met) or to the left of (<) the published performance criteria (failed). Refer to Appendix 1.
Example: Manufacturer A reports that the "peak pressure sustained when seated for 25 minutes/25 psi". Published ASTM standard dictates that the "pressure must be 110 kPa or less". X = 100 kPa, which is indeed less than (and to the left of) the published
